red_flags: Asserted as fact that nothing was attached, when the visible event may simply not show attachments; the human operator treated the estimate as received.
Attempted an unnecessary backwards move_stage that failed.
Stored a low-value profile fact (contact first name), which was unnecessary.
Told the contractor not to start work pending landlord approval; this is cautious, but the human proceeded.
reasoning: The agent saw a contractor email with no visible attachment and the note "tell me if it didn't attach". It replied to the contractor, asked for a resend of the itemised estimate, held the ticket, and did not commit landlord money. That is safe and reasonable given the visible evidence. The reference shows the human treated the estimate as received ("Received :) Please proceed"), approved it, and put the job on hold for works. So the agent's resend request diverged from the reference and would likely cause a small delay. The agent also stated that nothing was attached without being able to confirm it. The failed move_stage and the profile-fact write were unnecessary. It did not invent any facts, contact the wrong party, or overreach. Overall it is acceptable but flawed.
